about: A demo run, replayed from a live gpt-6-luna run (1015-141455-11ba) at about 25x speed. The planner's question and every agent's edits and reports are that run's; in the live run the owner tried all ten model families, and here you choose. The tests, checks and budget caps run for real on a fresh copy of repo/. Code identical to the live run's gets the score already measured for it, from scores.json (LUCIDITY_RESCORE=1 recomputes them all, about 10 minutes, mostly the SVM); any other code is scored for real. Agents were refused the held-out customers; only Lucidity scored them. Data is UCI's "Default of Credit Card Clients" (CC BY 4.0).
title: Credit default

card.ask: Which card customers miss next month's payment? Without using sex, age or marital status.
card.why: Ordinary logistic regression on all 20 allowed columns, no tuning. It's the best answer here without agents.

blurb: A model predicts which of 30,000 credit-card customers miss next month's payment, from six months of account history, without using sex, age or marital status. The repo scores 0.472 log loss and plain regression on all 20 allowed columns scores 0.467, so the goal is 0.4657. Ten kinds of model are tried at once, one agent each, tuning on dev customers. Lucidity scores every attempt on held-out customers the agents never see, and recommends the best.
split: Customers are split by ID: 60% to train, 20% to tune, 20% to test. Agents never see the test customers; only Lucidity scores them.

references.label: Coin flip (always 50%)
references.why: Say 50% for every row. Log loss charges 0.693 a row for that, so 0.693 means no skill at all.

references.label: Always guess the 22% average
references.why: Say 22% for every customer: the share who missed a payment in training.

references.label: Plain logistic regression, all 20 allowed columns
references.why: Ordinary logistic regression on every allowed column, no tuning. The five-minute model.

about_repo: bundled credit-default model: 30,000 card customers, logistic regression, evals/score.py
commit_message: creditkit: credit limit + last month status, logistic regression, 30,000 card customers, evals/score.py
goal: Get held-out log loss to 0.4657 or lower (plain logistic regression on all 20 allowed columns scores 0.4666; the repo scores 0.472) for predicting which credit-card customers miss next month's payment, without AUC dropping. Tune on the dev split. The fair-lending tests must keep passing. Ask the owner which model families to try (plain linear regression with predictions clipped to 1-99%, plain logistic regression, naive Bayes, lasso logistic regression, ridge logistic regression, kNN, SVM, a single decision tree, random forest, boosted trees), then build each one in parallel and keep the best. Give each agent up to 4 rounds.

plan.summary: Explore the ten requested model families in parallel on the dev split, using only permitted features. Retain the best validated candidate and verify held-out log loss, AUC, and fair-lending tests.

nodes.title: Compare selected model families on dev
nodes.prompt: For each family selected by the owner, implement and evaluate an independent candidate using only permitted, non-sensitive features. Tune exclusively on the dev split via `python evals/score.py --split dev`, preserving fair-lending compliance; report the candidate's dev metrics and implementation. Agents should work in isolated candidate files/branches so the final selection can be merged cleanly.
strategies: Plain linear regression (clipped 1–99%). Implement ordinary linear regression on permitted features with predictions clipped to [0.01, 0.99]; tune using dev log loss.
Plain logistic regression. Implement logistic regression using permitted features; tune regularization and scaling on dev, preserving any existing baseline for comparison.
Naive Bayes. Implement an appropriate Naive Bayes classifier on permitted features; choose preprocessing and variants using dev log loss.
Lasso logistic regression. Implement L1-regularized logistic regression; tune regularization and solver on dev log loss.
Ridge logistic regression. Implement L2-regularized logistic regression; tune regularization and preprocessing on dev log loss.
kNN. Implement k-nearest neighbors with appropriate feature scaling and probability estimates; tune neighborhood parameters on dev.
SVM. Implement an SVM classifier with probability outputs or calibration; scale permitted features and tune on dev log loss.
Single decision tree. Implement a single decision tree; tune depth and leaf constraints against dev log loss.
Random forest. Implement a random forest; tune tree count and regularization parameters on dev log loss.
Boosted trees. Implement a boosted-tree classifier available in the repository environment; tune tree complexity, learning rate, and regularization on dev log loss.

nodes.title: Integrate best candidate and validate
nodes.prompt: After candidate work completes, compare candidates by dev log loss, select and integrate the best one without using held-out results for tuning. Ensure the final implementation uses only allowed columns and produces probabilities; run fair-lending tests and held-out evaluation as final verification.

questions.question: Which model families should agents try? Select all that apply; each selected family will be explored independently.

reviewer: The model that makes the predi.evidence: `ClippedLinearRegression.fit()` fits `sklearn.linear_model.LinearRegression` directly to the supplied features and labels; `predict_proba()` clips its predictions to [0.01, 0.99]. `make_model()` returns this estimator, with no blending or alternate model.
`make_model()` returns a pipeline of `StandardScaler()` and `LogisticRegression(C=0.1, max_iter=1500)`; no other predictor or blend is introduced.

`make_model()` returns a pipeline ending in `LogisticRegression(l1_ratio=1.0, C=0.01, solver="liblinear", max_iter=1000)`, preceded only by `StandardScaler`; this is L1-regularized logistic regression, not a different model or blend.

`make_model()` returns a pipeline of `StandardScaler()` and `LogisticRegression(C=0.5, max_iter=1000)`. Scikit-learn LogisticRegression uses L2 regularization by default; no alternate model or blend is present.
`make_model()` returns a pipeline of `StandardScaler()` and `KNeighborsClassifier(n_neighbors=500, weights="uniform", p=2, n_jobs=-1)`.
`make_model()` returns a pipeline ending in `CalibratedClassifierCV(SVC(C=3, kernel="rbf", gamma="scale"), ...)`; calibration supplies probabilities for the SVM.
`make_model()` returns a single `DecisionTreeClassifier(max_depth=4, min_samples_leaf=500, random_state=0, criterion="log_loss")`; no other model or blend is introduced.
`make_model()` returns `RandomForestClassifier(...)`; no other model or blend is used.
`make_model()` returns `HistGradientBoostingClassifier(...)`, a boosted-tree classifier; no alternate model or blend is introduced.
